newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN: rollover on Iraq oil deal not in doubt.
newsitem.headline: UN: rollover on Iraq oil deal not in doubt.

text.p: A rollover of the oil-for-food plan for Iraq is a "foregone conclusion" presumably at the current $2 billion level, a senior U.N. official said Thursday.
Yasushi Akashi, undersecretary-general for humanitarian affairs, told reporters that renewal of the plan was virtually assured at current sales levels.

A senior U.N. official told Reuters on Wednesday that U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan was expected to recommend by the end of the month that the deal be renewed in June on the same terms as the present six-month plan.
Akashi made the comments on his way to the Security Council where he will brief members on his recent trip to Iraq which he described as "positive."
However, he gave no indication on when Annan would report to the council, which has to adopt a new resolution by June 7 when the current six-month plan expires.

The accord allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months in order to purchase food, medicine and other goods for its people suffering under U.N. sanctions imposed when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
About two-thirds of the monies are for the humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.

Iraq has complained frequently that the council's procedures had prevented the supplies from reaching the country within a reasonable period of time while oil sales moved quickly. Akashi's department is in charge of sending U.N. staff to Iraq to monitor the supplies.
According to U.N. officials, most governments support an extension of the current arrangements.

One envoy said that the United States had suggested some changes in dealing with Kurdish areas in the north, which have a separate allotment of food and medicine. But diplomats said no formal or informal proposal had been made by Washington.
